If you want free as in beer, the only real solution is hosting at home paired with dyndns. If you're willing to spend a little bit of money, a whole lot of options are open to you: shared hosting, virtual dedicated, colo, cloud... they can all be as cheap as a few dollars a month to several hundred, depending on the features you want.

If you're not going to host at home, and you've already decided to spend money, then the next decision to make is how you want to manage your site. If you want full, root-level access to all the systems so you can play with them, then you want virtual dedicated hosting; there are a ton of really cheap options for this, but do your research on them, because some have terrible support. If you don't want to have to manage the actual host, but you still want some level of control over the apps and configs, then you want colo; this is considerably more expensive, and not many people go for it these days. If you want something in between, with highly variable costs, then look to the cloud; there are a lot of providers out there, but AWS and Azure are the ones you want to get familiar with if you intend to spin this experience off into any kind of tangible career-related rewards down the line.

Shared hosting is the typical gold standard for these types of setups, though, and most big-name registrars offer this service these days for just a few dollars per month. GoDaddy, specifically, has offered full management of your shared host via CPanel for a couple of years now, as I recall, and allows for push-button setup of pretty much everything you need.
